item.title: Live: Mudslide hits Xizang border port, causing casualties
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-27
President Xi Jinping urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang Level-II emergency response activated after mudslide hits border port in Xizang President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out rescue and relief efforts after a mudslide on Wednesday in Nepal caused heavy casualties and left many people missing at a border port in the Xizang autonomous region. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the instruction after the mudslide struck the Gyirong border port, a major land port linking China and Nepal, in Shigatse at around 10:30 am, according to Xinhua News Agency. As of 8 pm on Wednesday, at least three people had been killed and 265 others remained missing, CCTV News quoted local authorities as saying. The president stressed that the top priority now is to make every possible effort to search for and rescue missing people, evacuate residents at risk and provide timely medical treatment to the injured. He also underlined efforts to strengthen monitoring and early warning, carry out rescue work in a scientific manner and prevent secondary disasters. Noting that the country is at a critical stage of flood control, Xi emphasized that all local authorities and relevant departments should prepare for worst-case scenarios and extreme situations, and earnestly implement measures for flood and typhoon prevention. They must also step up efforts to identify and defuse potential risks and hazards, resolutely prevent serious and major disasters and accidents, and effectively protect people's lives and property, he said. Premier Li Qiang has ordered prompt efforts to verify the number of people missing and affected, conduct all-out relief operations and evacuate people at risk. He urged the Foreign Ministry to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant countries to share information in a timely manner and work together to properly handle rescue and relief efforts. Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing has led a team to the site to guide rescue and response efforts. Video footage released by China Central Television showed muddy water gushing, carrying tree branches and debris, and some buildings were buried as the mudslide struck. Meanwhile, the disaster has cut off roads, communication networks and power supplies at the border port area on the Chinese side, Xinhua reported. In the wake of the disaster, China has activated a Level-II emergency response for disaster relief and a Level-II emergency response for geological disasters, the second-highest in the country's four-tier emergency response system. Governments at all levels have responded with immediate measures, making every effort to carry out disaster relief as well as search and rescue operations. Three central government departments — the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Emergency Management and the National Development and Reform Commission — have altogether allocated 220 million yuan ($33 million) to support Xizang in carrying out emergency rescue and disaster relief work. The Ministry of Emergency Management has deployed 249 personnel from the national comprehensive fire and rescue force, along with 325 engineering rescue personnel from China Anneng Construction Group, PowerChina and other centrally administered State-owned enterprises. A total of 30,000 central relief items, including tents, stoves, clothing and quilts, folding beds and moisture-proof mats, have been sent to support the evacuation, resettlement and relief work. At the local level, as of Wednesday afternoon, the Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps had deployed 72 vehicles and 431 fire and rescue personnel at the site, equipped with rescue dogs, life detectors, assault boats and other rescue equipment. Five repair workers from the State Grid Xizang Electric Power Co — the first group of emergency power repair personnel to arrive at the site — rushed there with a medium-voltage power generator vehicle and two small emergency lamps, and started work to ensure basic power supply and lighting for nighttime rescue operations. The local meteorological bureau has forecast continued rainfall across the county of Gyirong from Wednesday evening through Sunday, warning of possible floods, landslides and other secondary disasters in low-lying areas. LHASA -- Rescue teams are racing to a mudslide-stricken border port in southwest China's Xizang autonomous region after the disaster caused significant casualties along the China-Nepal border on Wednesday, local authorities said. A mudslide occurred on Wednesday morning in Nepal, resulting in three people dead and 265 missing at Gyirong Port in Gyirong county of Xizang as of 8 pm, according to initial estimates. Xizang has activated its highest-level relief and emergency response for natural disasters. The region's emergency management authority has dispatched 792 personnel and 152 vehicles for the rescue effort, while the regional fire and rescue authority has mobilized 72 vehicles and 431 firefighting and rescue personnel with rescue dogs, life scanners and speed boats to aid the effort. The local People's Liberation Army and armed police have also sent rescue and relief teams to the scene. As of 5:35 pm, central and regional authorities had dispatched relief supplies including 8,000 cotton coats, 2,000 tents, 3,000 quilts and 5,000 moisture-proof mats to the affected area, officials said. The mudslide has cut off roads leading to the port on the Chinese side, as well as communications and power supplies, officials revealed, adding that the first batch of power grid repairers had arrived at the site. On the national level, the Ministry of Natural Resources activated a Level-II emergency response for geological disasters, the second-highest in China's four-tier emergency response system, and dispatched a working team to the stricken site to guide rescue operations and prevent secondary disasters, the ministry said. The National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief, together with the Ministry of Emergency Management (MEM), helped allocate 30,000 central relief supplies including tents, stoves, clothing, quilts, folding beds and moisture-proof mats to support the evacuation, resettlement and relief work. The Ministry of Finance and the MEM also allocated 120 million yuan (about $17.69 million) in central natural disaster relief funds to support Xizang in carrying out emergency rescue and disaster relief operations. Meanwhile, the National Development and Reform Commission earmarked 100 million yuan in central budget investment to support post-disaster emergency recovery and reconstruction efforts. The local meteorological observatory forecasts continued rainfall across Gyirong County from Wednesday evening through Sunday, warning of possible floods, landslides and other secondary disasters in low-lying areas. The Western Theater Command Air Force of the Chinese People's Liberation Army dispatched a drone on Wednesday evening to survey disaster conditions in the Gyirong Port area of Xizang autonomous region, after a mudslide on the Nepal side of the border left at least three dead and 265 missing. The command sent the drone to the affected area for aerial reconnaissance at around 8 pm, after an airport on the plateau saw a brief spell of stable weather. The mudslide occurred at around 10:30 am on Wednesday, affecting Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Shigatse city. After the disaster, the Western Theater Command Air Force quickly activated its emergency response plan for disaster relief, with missions planned including aerial reconnaissance, search and rescue, and air transport, while organizing transport aircraft, helicopters, and drones to prepare for possible deployment. An army border defense regiment activated its flood control and rescue emergency plan immediately after the disaster. The Shigatse detachment of the People's Armed Police Force Xizang Contingent also launched an emergency response. According to reconnaissance by an advance team, roads and communications around Gyirong Port have been cut off, and some buildings have been buried. As of 5 pm on Wednesday, the Xizang Military Command had sent a forward command team to the site and urgently deployed emergency rescue forces. More than 130 troops from a unit under the Shigatse military sub-command, along with engineering machinery, had completed preparations for deployment. Meanwhile, more than 140 officers and soldiers from the Shigatse detachment of the People's Armed Police Force Xizang Contingent, carrying professional disaster relief equipment, were heading to the front line for rescue operations. A mudslide disaster affecting Gyirong county in Shigatse, Xizang autonomous region, has left three people dead and 265 others missing as of 8 pm local time on Wednesday, Xinhua News Agency reported. It said the figures were released by the front-line command center after preliminary verification. The exact number of casualties is still being checked, and rescue operations are proceeding in an orderly manner. The mudslide occurred at around 10:30 am on the Nepalese side of the border, affecting Gyirong port in Gyirong county, Shigatse, causing significant casualties and resulting in many people going missing. The mudslide also cut off roads leading toward Gyirong port, according to the report. The first group of emergency power repair personnel has arrived at Gyirong Port in Shigatse city, Xizang autonomous region, following a fatal mudslide on Wednesday, according to State Grid Xizang Electric Power Co. Five repair workers, one medium-voltage generator vehicle, and two small emergency lighting units are now in place to provide basic electricity and nighttime lighting for rescue operations, Xizang Television reported. More emergency power and lighting equipment, including mobile lighting towers, handheld lights, charging units, low-voltage generator vehicles, and small generators, is being sent to the disaster-hit area. The company has also allocated lightweight utility poles and other repair materials, while another 20 professional repair workers are heading to the site to help restore power lines damaged by the disaster. The mudslide occurred at around 10:30 am on Wednesday on the Nepal side of the border and caused large numbers of casualties and left people missing at Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Shigatse. Roads to the port were cut off, while power and communications were disrupted, according to local authorities. KATHMANDU - As many as 72 people have been found dead in the flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal, police said. Abi Narayan Kafle, spokesperson of Nepal Police, confirmed to Xinhua, adding that 41 injured people have been receiving treatment in different hospitals. China's Xizang autonomous region activated a Level I emergency response for natural disasters on Wednesday after a mudslide that began in Nepal resulted in significant numbers of casualties and missing. The mudslide occurred at around 10:30 am, according to the regional emergency command, eventually hitting Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Shigatse city, close to the border with Nepal. Authorities have launched search and rescue operations, evacuation and resettlement of affected residents, while the injured are being treated. Monitoring for secondary disasters is being carried out, while emergency supplies are also being dispatched and rescue forces deployed to support relief work. Shigatse city in Xizang autonomous region activated a Level I emergency response for natural disaster relief on Wednesday afternoon after a mudslide caused casualties and left people missing in the Gyirong Port area of Gyirong county. The disaster was triggered by a mudslide on the Nepalese side of the border, with the impact felt in the port area of China's Shigatse city. Casualties and missing were confirmed by the city's emergency command office, with rescue workers dispatched to the area. Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps deployed 431 firefighters, 72 vehicles, search and rescue dogs, life detectors and inflatable boats to the scene on Wednesday afternoon, according to Xizang Television. LHASA - Two-way temporary traffic restrictions have been put in place on roads leading to Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, after a mudslide struck near the border port on Wednesday morning, local traffic authorities said. All routes from Gyirong town to the port are closed to vehicles except for emergency and rescue operations until further notice, according to local authorities. The restrictions were imposed after the mudslide rendered roads in the port area unsafe for travel, and cut off road links, communications and power supplies to the Chinese side of the port, the emergency management bureau of Gyirong county in Shigatse city said. The mudslide, which occurred on the Nepalese side, caused severe casualties and left people unaccounted for at Gyirong Port. The local meteorological observatory forecasts continued rainfall across the county from Wednesday evening through Sunday, warning of possible floods, landslides and other secondary disasters in low-lying areas. Gyirong Port is a major land port linking China and Nepal. KATHMANDU - The death toll from a massive flash flood in Nepal's Bhote Koshi River on Wednesday reached 22, the police said. Rajendra Prasad Dhamala, spokesperson for the Bagmati Province Police, confirmed the death toll and said search and rescue operations were continuing in the affected areas. Security forces have so far rescued 88 people from the affected areas, Dhamala said. The Nepal Tourism Board said that as many as 384 tourists, including 291 foreigners, have been reported missing after a massive flash flood swept through Rasuwa district in northern Nepal. Sunil Sharma, spokesperson at the board, said the missing foreign tourists were from India, Australia, the Netherlands, the United States, Malaysia, Britain and South Africa, among others. Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called an emergency cabinet meeting to discuss rescue and relief measures. The Nepali Army, backed by other security forces, has intensified search and rescue operations in the affected districts. The worst damage has been reported in Rasuwa, where the flood swept away several houses, damaging markets, hydropower projects, roads and other infrastructure. "Several people are reported missing. Rescue efforts are underway," Druba Prasad Adhikari, deputy chief district officer of Rasuwa, told Xinhua earlier. A mudslide that began in Nepal caused heavy casualties at Gyirong border port in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday morning. The National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction, and Relief and the Ministry of Emergency Management have activated a Level-II national disaster relief emergency response, the second-highest in China's four-tier natural disaster relief system. This response is reserved for major and extremely serious disasters and was activated after a mudslide in Nepal caused casualties at the Gyirong border port in southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday morning. A mudslide caused significant casualties and left people missing at the Gyirong border port in Gyirong county, Shigatse, in Xizang, around 10:30 am on Wednesday. This prompted China to dispatch 574 rescue personnel, allocate 30,000 disaster relief supplies, and earmark 120 million yuan in central disaster relief funds for emergency response and rescue work. Following the disaster, the Ministry of Emergency Management immediately coordinated rescue and relief efforts and sent a work team to the site to assist with the emergency response. The rescue forces include 249 personnel from the national comprehensive fire and rescue force and 325 engineering rescuers from China Anneng Group, PowerChina, and other units, who were dispatched with equipment. Specialized equipment, including emergency communication support systems and aeromagnetic detection devices, has also been sent to the disaster area to support on-site communications, search operations, and rescue work. The Ministry of Natural Resources also activated a Level-II geological disaster prevention response at 3 pm on Wednesday and sent a work team to the site to guide rescue operations and help guard against secondary geological disasters. The ministry urged the Xizang regional natural resources department to immediately send an expert team to assist local authorities with search and rescue, emergency response, and technical support. It also called for increased inspections, monitoring, early warning, and prevention work against similar geological risks. The China Geological Survey and the ministry's technical guidance center for geological disasters have been asked to strengthen expert coordination, consultation, and risk assessment to provide full technical support for front-line rescue work. Together with the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, authorities allocated 30,000 central disaster relief supplies, including tents, heating stoves, clothing, quilts, folding beds, and moisture-proof mats, to support the relocation and resettlement of affected residents. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management urgently pre-allocated 120 million yuan ($17.9 million) in central natural disaster relief funds to support Xizang in emergency rescue and relief work. The funds will be used mainly for search and rescue, relocation and resettlement of affected residents, risk removal, emergency response, and the repair of damaged homes to minimize disaster losses and casualties. Weather conditions may add pressure to rescue work. From Wednesday evening to Sunday, most parts of Gyirong county are forecast to see light to moderate rain or thunderstorms, while some low-altitude townships in the south may experience heavy rain, local meteorological authorities said. Low-altitude areas of the county face a heightened risk of rain-triggered disasters, with mountain torrents, mudslides, and landslides possible in some places. Thunderstorms, gales, hail, and short-term heavy rainfall are also likely from afternoon to night in various areas, posing further disaster risks, local meteorological authorities said. The Xizang regional meteorological bureau has entered a special working mode and is updating weather forecasts every two hours to support front-line disaster relief operations. Chinese authorities have mobilized emergency relief materials to support rescue and resettlement work in Xizang autonomous region after a cross-border debris flow caused a large number of casualties and missing persons. At around 10:30 am on Wednesday, a debris flow occurred on the Nepalese side of the border, which continued across into Gyirong Port in Gyirong county, Shigatse. Since then, the Office of the National Committee for Disaster Reduction and Relief, the Ministry of Emergency Management, together with the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, has allocated 30,000 items of central government disaster relief supplies to the affected area. The materials include tents, heating stoves, quilts and clothes, folding beds, moisture-proof mats and other daily necessities and disaster-rescue equipment, which will support the resettlement of affected residents and aid targeted disaster assistance work. Also on Wednesday, the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management allocated 120 million yuan ($18 million) in natural disaster relief funds to support Xizang. The focus is on search and rescue operations, relocating and resettling affected residents, eliminating hazards, and repairing damaged homes. The National Development and Reform Commission allocated 100 million yuan on Wednesday to support the emergency restoration and reconstruction of infrastructure and other facilities in the disaster-affected areas. He made the instructions after a mudslide occurred at around 10:30 am on Wednesday in Nepal, which caused severe casualties and left people unaccounted for at Gyirong border port in Gyirong county. Noting that China is currently in a critical period of flood control, he urged local authorities and relevant departments to prepare for worst-case scenarios and extreme situations, fully implement measures for flood and typhoon prevention, and step up efforts to identify and address potential risks and hazards. He demanded resolute action to prevent major and catastrophic disasters and accidents and safeguard people's lives and property. Premier Li Qiang also issued instructions, calling for an immediate verification of the number of the missing and affected people and for all-out rescue and relief efforts. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, instructed the Foreign Ministry to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant countries, promptly share information and work together to properly handle rescue and relief efforts. Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, led officials from relevant departments to the site to guide rescue and disaster-response operations. Authorities in Xizang have mobilized forces to carry out search and rescue operations. All relevant operations are underway. A landslide struck near Gyirong Port in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Wednesday and some people may be missing, according to local authorities. The county-level emergency management bureau in Gyirong, administered by Shigatse, said the landslide occurred near the border port, which serves as a major land crossing between China and Nepal. Access roads, telecommunications, and power supply on the Chinese side have been cut off, the bureau said. Emergency response teams have been mobilized to the affected area. Further details are being verified as rescue operations continue.

item.title: AI can restore confidence, unlock growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
AI can restore confidence, unlock growth The International Monetary Fund in July projected 4.6 percent growth for the Chinese economy in 2026, one of the strongest results among major economies. China's economy has also demonstrated considerable resilience in the first half of the year, with GDP expanding 4.7 percent year-on-year despite a challenging global environment. Yet some Western economists remain skeptical of China's growth path, citing structural concerns including an overreliance on trade rather than domestic demand and adjustments in sectors such as steel, electric vehicles and solar panels. But what both official and independent readings agree on is that households, enterprises and local governments have all become more measured about spending, investing and borrowing. One possible key lever to spur growth is boosting the willingness of households, businesses and local governments to spend, invest and borrow again. And a new cluster of technologies — smart manufacturing, space technology, the low-altitude economy, robotics, big data and, above all, artificial intelligence — is helping to build that confidence and create new opportunities for growth. A global comparison helps explain why these technologies, AI especially, carry this weight. Global capital is increasingly recognizing the transformative potential of AI and related technologies. The point is not which company is "better", but what the gap reveals: Global capital now assigns trillion-dollar valuations almost overnight to companies considered to be at the frontier of AI, in a way it never did for the previous tech cycle's retail and software platforms. China's growth model has long rested on three engines: exports (about 20 percent of GDP in 2024), household consumption (around 39.9 percent), and gross capital formation — the broad measure covering investment and infrastructure — at roughly 40.6 percent. These figures capture the distinctive structure described above: Investment remains unusually high by international standards, consumption comparatively low. Exports still perform well, aided by industrial scale and diversification toward Europe and Latin America that has offset the weaker demand of the United States, but investment-led growth is harder to sustain as infrastructure can no longer serve as an unlimited stabilization tool. Greater confidence should be built in consumption. Retail sales rose 3.7 percent in 2025, online retail increased 8.6 percent, and final consumption contributed 52 percent of GDP growth — five points more than the year before. That is a meaningful shift, but not yet a full substitute for property-led growth. History offers a guide. Japan after 1990 showed that even near-zero rates cannot force households focused on repairing balance sheets to spend. China's own reform era is more encouraging: Deng Xiaoping's 1992 Southern Tour shifted expectations so decisively that real fixed investment rose 28.2 percent that year. Confidence returns when policy signals are sustained. China's own experience demonstrates how stronger expectations can unlock investment, entrepreneurship and economic activity. This is where AI — and the wider array of frontier technologies now emerging in China — becomes economically relevant, not as a symbol but as a potential fourth engine reinforcing the other three. In exports, it can lift manufacturing productivity and push companies into higher-value segments, as Chinese labs such as DeepSeek have shown they can already do on the global stage. China's world-class manufacturing base gives it a strong platform for turning AI advances into productivity gains across the real economy. In investment, it can redirect capital from basic infrastructure toward computing power and data centers — the very assets global markets now reward with premium valuations. In consumption, it can open up demand in healthcare, education and digital services, while creating new products, services and employment opportunities for households. The scale on display at the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, backed by evident State commitment, signals this is a growth strategy, not a side project. Technology alone cannot inject confidence in all sectors. Turning that into domestic confidence still requires more active policy support — so that AI-driven growth becomes secure jobs and rising incomes, and eventually stronger household confidence and consumption. China's transition can be summarized simply: In the earlier growth phase, expansion generated confidence; in the phase ahead, confidence will have to generate expansion. An economy with real capacity and increasingly sophisticated sources of innovation and growth, is still working to fully unlock the confidence needed to put that capacity to work. AI, if it can convert conference-hall momentum into household-level trust, may be the engine that helps supply it. The author is a former tourism minister of Brazil, a distinguished professor at Tsinghua University and a professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong in Shenzhen. The views do not necessarily reflect those of China Daily. item.title: What is behind Shein's drop in valuation?
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
What is behind Shein's drop in valuation? Shein's Hong Kong IPO is testing how public investors value a global e-commerce model being reshaped by slower growth, rising fulfillment costs and tighter rules for low-value parcels, industry experts said. At the top of the proposed HK$47.6 ($6.07) to HK$49.5 range, Shein would have a market capitalization of up to $27 billion, roughly 70 percent below its nearly $100 billion private valuation in 2022. Pan Helin, a member of the expert committee for information and communication economy under the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, attributed the valuation reset partly to the maturity of e-commerce, where growth has slowed and competition has intensified. "Shein's rapid rise in 2022 coincided with overseas supply-chain disruptions and sharp price increases, while today's market conditions leave less room for the exceptional growth expectations reflected in its earlier private valuation," Pan said. Pan added that Hong Kong investors generally apply more restrained valuations to mature internet businesses, particularly apparel e-commerce, which operates in a largely established market. Capital has also recently shifted toward artificial intelligence-related companies, further limiting the valuation premium available to traditional e-commerce platforms, he said. Although HK-listed e-commerce and internet companies are currently trading at relatively low valuations, a Hong Kong listing could help Shein reduce the compliance risks associated with cross-border fundraising and facilitate its domestic operations, Pan noted. "It would give Shein access to a market recognized by international investors while also bringing it closer to domestic investors, particularly as the Chinese mainland could become a more important growth market for the company in the future," he said. Pan's comments came as overseas policy changes have added to the company's operating pressure. The United States ended duty-free de minimis treatment in May 2025 for covered goods from the Chinese mainland and Hong Kong that had previously entered in parcels valued at no more than $800. From July 1 this year, the European Union also abolished its customs-duty exemption for consignments valued at no more than 150 euros ($175) and introduced a temporary duty of 3 euros per item category. The e-commerce giant is responding by shifting from its previous direct-to-consumer shipping model into a more flexible business-to-business-to-consumer pattern — consolidating goods in China, shipping them to Europe in bulk and completing delivery from local warehouses, said Chen Liteng, a senior analyst at the Internet Economy Institute, a domestic consultancy. "This model subjects the goods to the EU's regular apparel import tariffs instead of a flat duty on each item category," Chen said. "Even after adding the cost of sorting, packing and local delivery, the model's total cost remains below the per-category duty incurred by direct shipment of small parcels." The senior analyst added that the use of local warehouses could also reduce customs-related costs while allowing Shein to retain the inventory discipline of its signature "test-and-repeat" model, under which products are initially made in small batches and replenished according to demand. The IPO comprises about 280 million Class B shares. At the midpoint, without over-allotment, net proceeds are expected to reach HK$13.1 billion. According to its prospectus, the company has earmarked 40 percent for technology capabilities, 40 percent for brand building and global expansion, 10 percent for corporate responsibility and the balance for general purposes. lijiaying@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Food system resilience in APEC's focus
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
Food system resilience in APEC's focus Hangzhou meeting calls for greater use of innovation, digital tech to tackle risks Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation economies adopted on Tuesday principles aimed at strengthening the resilience of food systems through innovation and digitalization, as extreme weather, supply chain disruptions and rising production costs pose growing challenges to agriculture across the region. The Joint Statement on the 11th APEC Food Security Ministerial Meeting and the Principles for Strengthening Food Systems Resilience in the APEC Region through Innovation and Digitalization were adopted at the meeting in Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province. According to officials at the meeting, the principles call for the greater use of innovation and digital technologies to strengthen food systems, improve agricultural productivity and help economies respond to risks, including those posed by extreme weather. Vice-Premier Liu Guozhong emphasized that APEC plays a pivotal role in maintaining global food security. He added that China is willing to work with other economies to jointly build a more robust food security system. Liu called for stronger innovation-driven efforts and deeper agricultural science and technology cooperation to jointly cultivate new ways of safeguarding food security. Eduardo Pedrosa, executive director of the APEC Secretariat, said that food security has become one of the defining challenges. "Extreme weather, supply chain disruptions and rising fertilizer and fuel costs are all adding uncertainty for farmers, rural communities, producers, and consumers in an interconnected region," Pedrosa said. Innovation is central to APEC's efforts to strengthen food systems, improve productivity and help farmers adapt to changing conditions through digital technologies, artificial intelligence and agricultural biotechnology, he said. "The principles for strengthening food systems resilience through innovation and digitalization reflect our shared commitment to ensuring the technologies serve people and empowering food security," said Pedrosa. However, ensuring that new technologies benefit farmers will require measures to close the digital divide among different economies in the region that are at different stages, Pedrosa said. In the immediate future, APEC economies should also focus on facilitating food trade and reducing losses along supply chains, he added. Carlos Vasquez, Peruvian ambassador to China, said that research and development, innovation and digitalization should be priority areas for agricultural cooperation in the region. He said that the intensive application of digital technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, could help economies mitigate uncertainty from extreme weather events such as the potentially strongest-ever El Nino later this year. "We should increase our mutual cooperation in the forum regarding the very important need of applying new digital technologies to improve the resilience of our food systems," Vasquez said. Meanwhile, smallholder farmers, who are the backbone of the agricultural system in Peru, need greater access to digital training, finance and infrastructure. "It's going to be a combination of the intensive application of digital technologies plus the development of key infrastructure for them to be connected to markets," the ambassador said. Nelson Simbiken, director-general of Papua New Guinea's National Agricultural Research Institute, said that APEC economies should use digital tools to map different ecosystems and develop smart farming systems suited to local conditions. Simbiken also called for greater data sharing and cooperation in areas including environmental sustainability and agricultural planning. zhaoyimeng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: US ups unilateral sanctions on Iran
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
US ups unilateral sanctions on Iran Tensions: Sanctions seen as threat to world The United States imposed a new wave of sanctions on Iran on Monday, which it said would cut off the economic lifeline that sustains the country. Experts said the move appears unlikely to force Tehran to bow down, but will further strain the global economy. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a news release on Monday that the new sectoral sanctions target five critical sectors: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. According to the department, starting on Monday, "the actions of Treasury and other agencies will tighten the noose and block every potential source of revenue that funds the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iranian regime". The department added that countries and entities continuing to do business with Iran will face heightened secondary sanctions risks. "Every country has a defined timeline to shut down activities we have identified. If they do not take action, we will do so unilaterally through Treasury authorities," it said. "Any entity that facilitates money laundering on behalf of Iran will be removed from the US dollar system." China firmly opposed on Tuesday these illegal unilateral sanctions, which it said lack any basis in international law and the authorization of the United Nations Security Council. Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said at a regular news conference that China's cooperation with Iran has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be disrupted. The country will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests, he added. The spokesman stressed that economic warfare and maximum pressure will not help resolve the issue, but only further escalate tensions, create spillover risks, disrupt the global economic and financial order, and harm the legitimate rights and interests of other countries. The top priority now is to ease the tensions and return to dialogue and negotiation as soon as possible, Lin said. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in his meeting on Monday in Tehran with Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir that the US must change its tone and approach in dealing with Iran, Mehr News agency reported. In a separate meeting with Munir on Monday, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said that Tehran remains determined to pursue implementation of the provisions of the US-Iran peace memorandum of understanding signed in June, Tasnim News Agency reported. Washington and Tehran have been at odds since the 1979 Islamic Revolution and the hostage crisis, in which Iranian students seized the US embassy in Tehran and took US diplomats hostage. Washington has imposed a slew of sanctions on Tehran and steadily expanded them over the past four decades. Experts said the latest move is likely to add fresh layers of disruption and complexity to the global economy and diplomatic efforts, particularly as Tehran maintains close communication with regional neighbors and mediators such as Oman and Pakistan. Jawaid Iqbal, vice-chancellor of Baba Ghulam Shah Badshah University in India, told China Daily that the US has been blowing hot and cold over the past several weeks with regard to Iran. "This in itself is proof that the US is not in a position to dictate its peace terms with Iran," Iqbal said. "The latest threat of sanctions shows that Washington is trying to somehow extricate itself from a messy situation of its own making." "Iran, on the other hand, will not bow down to Washington's terms and conditions so easily. It knows that by retaliating against America's regional allies, it can submerge the entire Gulf into chaos, which will in turn create turmoil in the world economy," he added. Deniz Istikbal, an assistant professor and economics researcher at Istanbul Medipol University in Turkiye, noted that the economic dimension of the Iran-US conflict is intensifying, posing challenges for the global economy. Conducting business with Iran is becoming increasingly challenging, as Washington seeks to isolate Tehran and push the government to the negotiating table by exerting financial pressure, he said. "These developments are making the conflict increasingly costly for the global economy, while interest rates are rising and inflation is once again becoming a major concern. "Ultimately, the cost of the conflict is creating additional burdens for the entire world, particularly for energy-importing countries, leading to higher taxation and increased borrowing needs," Istikbal noted. item.title: Fujian league attracts cross-Strait players
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
Fujian league attracts cross-Strait players Taiwan soccer talent find goals, massive crowds at mainland matches Editor's note: The Taiwan question is a key focus for China and the international community. China Daily is publishing a series of reports to track hot Taiwan-related topics and address disinformation from the Democratic Progressive Party administration. The Fujian city soccer league is inviting Taiwan players to compete on the Chinese mainland, and welcoming residents from across the Strait to enjoy the matches firsthand to deepen compatriot affinities and bring hearts closer together. Representing Fujian province's nine cities and the Pingtan Comprehensive Experimental Zone, 10 teams and nearly 500 amateur players are competing in the tournament, which will conclude with the final in October. To boost cross-Strait integration, Fujian — the primary ancestral home for Taiwan compatriots — allows every participating team to add two Taiwan players to its roster. By August, 19 Taiwan players had joined different city teams, according to the Fujian provincial administration of sport. Data show that more than 1,500 people from Taiwan have attended matches across Fujian, and that the league serves as an active catalyst for deepening cross-Strait people-to-people exchanges. Ni Pei-hsu, 24, from Taiwan, joined Fuzhou's soccer club in late June after learning about the recruitment online and was drawn by the massive crowds. It's his first time playing on the mainland.

item.title: Hunan scenic area boosts hot spot bona fides
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
Hunan scenic area boosts hot spot bona fides Wulingyuan's spiked peaks made famous in 2009 blockbuster movie Avatar On a theater stage framed by the towering sandstone peaks of Wulingyuan Scenic Area in Zhangjiajie, Hunan province, Pablo, a Spanish tourist, donned traditional Tujia wedding attire, playing the role of bridegroom as hundreds of spectators cheered. The mock ceremony at Charming Xiangxi Theater offered him an unforgettable introduction to local customs. For local business owners and operators, it represents something more strategic — a golden opportunity to attract tourist revenue after travelers descend from the world-famous Zhangjiajie peaks. "We had never seen a performance like this," Pablo said afterwards. "I would like to learn more about traditional Chinese culture." Across Zhangjiajie and neighboring historical towns in western Hunan, rising inbound arrivals are encouraging businesses to expand beyond scenic-area tickets into evening entertainment, accommodation, dining and cultural experiences. Official data underscore the momentum. Zhangjiajie welcomed 860,700 inbound visits from 195 countries and regions in the first seven months, up by 19.01 percent year-on-year. Tourism foreign-exchange earnings increased 40.52 percent to $98.5 million. The demographic profile of visitors is also undergoing a structural shift. European and US travelers accounted for nearly 35 percent of total inbound arrivals, with their numbers rising 211.36 percent year-on-year and helping diversify a market long dominated by travelers from South Korea. This surge has been powered in large part by China's expanding visa-free policies. China has expanded unilateral visa-free access to citizens of 50 countries for stays of up to 30 days, while nationals of 57 countries are eligible for its visa-free transit policy, following the addition of Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam on Thursday. Zhangjiajie Hehua International Airport is among the 65 designated ports for the transit policy. The airport operates 13 passenger routes to eight countries and regions, and long-haul travel Western visitors increasingly bundle the city into multi-stop itineraries across China. For years, Zhangjiajie's international acclaim rested largely on its quartz-sandstone pillars, famously associated with the floating mountains in the blockbuster 2009 film Avatar. Today, regional stakeholders view these iconic vistas merely as the starting point of an extended consumer journey. "The underlying business logic is to shift from one-off gate admissions to capturing spending across the entire travel chain as visitors extend their stays. Accommodation, dining, performances and immersive cultural experiences can all generate additional revenue," said Huang Yuanji, vice-president of Hunan University of Finance and Economics. At Charming Xiangxi Theater, which showcases the heritage of the Tujia, Miao and other ethnic groups, the number of overseas visitors reached 116,000 from 188 countries and regions between January and July, up 43 percent year-on-year. To bridge cultural divides, the theater provides subtitles in English and Korean, with Russian and Spanish in the works. Promotional materials have also been tailored. Traditional acrobatic acts, for example, are introduced using references to Chinese kung fu that foreign viewers intuitively grasp. "Foreign visitors might not know what Xiangxi is, but they know Zhangjiajie's mountains and are interested in authentic traditions. Our job is to interpret local heritage in ways they understand," said Xu Shan, general manager of the theater. A short distance away, Xiangxi Fu, a newly opened cultural tourism attraction in Wulingyuan, welcomes guests with traditional drum performances, ethnic folk songs and ceremonial welcome wine before ushering them into a courtyard complex dedicated to centuries of Tusi history. The attraction says foreign visitors account for 30 to 40 percent of its tourists. "Our goal is to transform static heritage exhibitions into participatory workshops and performances, giving visitors compelling reasons to linger in town after their mountain hikes," said Tang Linfang, the site's marketing director.

item.title: 'Sportcation' enthusiasts find place in the sun
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
'Sportcation' enthusiasts find place in the sun Younger generation flocks to Hainan coastal area for health, fun, activities and personal development Qi Huan has spent four years at a Shanghai tech company, commuting two hours to work every day. She is in seven work chat groups and her heart races every time her phone buzzes on weekends. One morning at 2 am, after finishing yet another business proposal, she stared at her screen for 10 minutes and decided on the spot to have a weeklong holiday. She immediately booked a flight to Sanya in Hainan province and a short time later arrived in the coastal city of Wanning by train. She had no itinerary or plan — just the knowledge that there was a "sports school" located there where people were active and energetic. In Wanning, she found what she was looking for. "Before, I worked like crazy so I could have a better life. Now I realize life shouldn't be about that," she said.

item.title: When kindness takes root, forests grow
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
When kindness takes root, forests grow Share - WeChat
Ronald Sakolsky, a retired teacher from the United States, returned to the home of China's afforestation hero, Yin Yuzhen, on Monday in Uxin Banner, Ordos, in the Inner Mongolia autonomous region. Back in 1999, while teaching in Luoyang, Sakolsky was moved by Yin's story of fighting desertification and donated $5,000 to the cause. She used the money to plant 50,000 trees, which have since grown into a towering forest in the Maowusu sandy area.
